statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns a result r, r is the maximum, over all valid hopping sequences p = (p_0, p_1, ..., p_m) with m >= 1, p_0 = 0, p_m = n - 1, and p_{k-1} < p_k for every k with 1 <= k <= m, of the score Σ_{k=1}^m (p_k - p_{k-1}) * nums[p_k].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, max_score(nums) returns Ok(r) for some i64 value r; it does not return an error, panic, overflow, or index out of bounds.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r, there exists at least one valid hopping sequence p = (p_0, ..., p_m) with m >= 1, p_0 = 0, p_m = n - 1, and p_{k-1} < p_k for every 1 <= k <= m, such that Σ_{k=1}^m (p_k - p_{k-1}) * nums[p_k] = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r, r <= (n - 1) * max{ nums[i] | 1 <= i < n }.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r, r >= Σ_{i=1}^{n-1} nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r >= i * nums[i] + (n - 1 - i) * nums[n - 1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r and max_score(nums') returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(nums'). Both slices satisfy 2 <= n <= 100000 and all their entries lie in [1,100000]. They agree at every index i with 1 <= i < n; the values nums[0] and nums'[0] may differ.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r and max_score(nums') returns r', we have r' >= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(nums'). Both slices satisfy 2 <= n <= 100000 and all their entries lie in [1,100000]. There is an index j with 1 <= j < n such that nums'[j] >= nums[j], and nums'[i] = nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n and i ≠ j.

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r and max_score(nums') returns r', we have r' = r + (n - 1) * c.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(nums'). Both slices satisfy 2 <= n <= 100000 and all their entries lie in [1,100000]. There is an integer c such that nums'[i] = nums[i] + c for every i with 1 <= i < n, and nums'[0] = nums[0].

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r and max_score(nums') returns r', we have r' = c * r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) = len(nums'). Both slices satisfy 2 <= n <= 100000 and all their entries lie in [1,100000]. There is an integer c >= 1 such that nums'[i] = c * nums[i] for every i with 1 <= i < n, and nums'[0] = nums[0].

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r, r = Σ_{i=1}^{n-1} nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000 and all entries lie in [1,100000]. For every i with 1 <= i < n - 1, nums[i] >= nums[i + 1].

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns r, r = (n - 1) * nums[n - 1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000 and all entries lie in [1,100000]. For every i with 1 <= i < n, nums[i] <= nums[n - 1].

statement: Whenever max_score(nums) returns Ok(r), r = sum_{i=1}^{n-1} max{ nums[j] | i <= j < n }.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The slice nums satisfies 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000.
